summary: The S. 3265 bill amends the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to extend, modify, and enhance the Work Opportunity Tax Credit through December 31, 2030. It adjusts credit percentages for first-year wages, adds inflation adjustments, alters rules for specific categories such as veterans and summer youth, removes certain age limits for food assistance recipients, expands eligibility to include qualified military spouses, and directs federal agencies to promote hiring targeted workers in critical industries.

affected_groups.effect: Eligible for revised and extended tax credits when hiring workers from targeted groups who begin work after December 31, 2025.
Subject to updated wage limitation calculations that determine the tax credit amounts available to employers who hire them.
Covered by updated first-year and second-year wage credit formulas.
Subject to revised credit calculation rules and wage limits.
Older individuals previously excluded by the age 40 cap become eligible for the credit.
affected_groups.group: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits recipients

affected_groups.effect: Added as a newly eligible targeted group for the credit.

key_provisions: Extends the expiration date of the Work Opportunity Tax Credit from December 31, 2025, to December 31, 2030.

Changes the first-year wage credit structure to 50 percent of qualified first-year wages up to $6,000, plus an additional 50 percent for wages between $6,000 and $12,000 for workers who complete at least 400 hours of service.
Adds annual inflation adjustments for base wage limits starting after 2025.
Updates wage limitations and formulas for certain veterans, long-term family assistance recipients, summer youth employees, and agricultural and railway labor.
Removes the upper age limit of 40 for qualified Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits recipients.
Adds spouses of members of the Armed Forces of the United States as a new targeted group eligible for the credit.

Directs the Secretary of the Treasury, Secretary of Commerce, Secretary of Labor, and Small Business Administration Administrator to promote hiring targeted group members in industries like manufacturing, infrastructure, energy, health care, and construction.
